name: Müllerian aplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnostic criteria for MRKH syndrome

criteria.description: Congenital absence or hypoplasia of the uterus and upper two-thirds of the vagina
Normal development of secondary sexual characteristics including normal ovarian function and normal external genitalia
Normal female karyotype (46,XX) without chromosomal abnormalities
Presence of renal tract anomalies such as unilateral renal agenesis or ectopic kidney
Associated skeletal abnormalities including vertebral anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital absence or hypoplasia of the uterus and upper vagina with normal secondary sexual characteristics and 46,XX karyotype
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is typically confirmed by imaging and karyotyping; genetic testing may be considered for syndromic cases.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital absence of upper two-thirds of vagina
Primary amenorrhea with normal secondary sexual characteristics
searchTerms: no menstruation despite normal puberty signs
primary amenorrhea with normal breasts and hair
no periods but normal secondary sexual features

common.symptomName: Normal ovarian function with regular hormonal profile
Unilateral renal agenesis or renal ectopia
searchTerms: single kidney or kidney in wrong place

occasional.symptomName: Hearing impairment due to associated otologic anomalies
searchTerms: hearing loss due to ear abnormalities
hearing impairment linked to otologic issues

occasional.symptomName: Mild skeletal malformations such as fused vertebrae
Urinary tract infections secondary to renal anomalies
searchTerms: urinary tract infections due to kidney issues

occasional.symptomName: Psychological distress related to infertility and diagnosis
searchTerms: mental health issues related to infertility

rare.symptomName: Cardiac malformations such as septal defects
searchTerms: heart defects like holes in septum

laboratory: Normal female hormonal profile (FSH, LH, estradiol)
imaging: Pelvic MRI or ultrasound showing absent or hypoplastic uterus and upper vagina
Renal ultrasound or MRI revealing renal anomalies
genetic: No consistent single gene mutation identified; some familial cases suggest genetic heterogeneity
Candidate genes under investigation include WNT4, HNF1B
other: Normal external genitalia on physical examination

distinguishingFeatures: Female external genitalia with absent uterus due to androgen receptor insensitivity
Presence of uterus and upper vagina

redFlags: Primary amenorrhea with absent uterus on imaging
Normal secondary sexual characteristics despite amenorrhea
Associated renal or skeletal anomalies detected on screening
